methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units of information. These units represent individual requirements, features, behaviors, constraints, and functional aspects of the gshare branch predictor. The decomposition aimed to create independent, self-contained, technically specific, and unambiguous units that could be assessed for coverage and similarity. Each atomic unit was designed to be implementable as a single, verifiable requirement. The original research topic was analyzed to identify all explicit and implicit requirements, while the generated specification was examined to extract all described functionalities and design elements. The goal was to create two sets (X and Y) of atomic information units that could be compared to determine the extent to which the generated specification covers the original research topic.
